title: The Promotion Nobody Celebrated

voiceProfile.tense: Past tense with acute, sharp present-tense corporate rhythms
voiceProfile.register: Lucid, analytical, unsentimental, forensic, carrying quiet emotional fatigue
voiceProfile.narratorDistance: Close third-person; tracking Meera's internal risk ledger as she evaluates both derivative trading algorithms and the collateral damage of her life
distinctiveDevices: Sidebar metrics: quarterly performance indicators, compensation schedules, headcount numbers contrasting with empty calendar blocks
Exact financial compensation figures and corporate tier levels (VP, SVP, Managing Director, Band 9)
The physical geography of modern corporate Gurgaon (Cyber City skybridges, Golf Course Road underpasses, 24-hour illuminated glass offices)

protagonist.name: Meera Nambiar
protagonist.family: Daughter of a retired State Bank of Travancore cashier in Thrissur; divorced eighteen months earlier from Ashwin (a documentary editor who couldn't bear the Gurgaon executive culture); younger brother Vivek (civil services aspirant in Trivandrum)
protagonist.education: B.Tech from College of Engineering Trivandrum (CET); MBA from a second-tier institute in Pune before breaking into institutional algorithmic trading through pure mathematical capability
protagonist.career: Promoted on the night of the story from Senior Vice President to Managing Director & Head of Quantitative Risk at Nexa Capital, Gurgaon
protagonist.income: New base salary ₹1.4 crore + annual performance stock units (RSUs) projected at ₹90 lakh
habits: Carries two phones; screen time averages 14 hours and 40 minutes per day
Eats roasted almonds from a glass jar in her office drawer instead of lunch
Wears custom charcoal trouser suits; has seven identical white Egyptian cotton shirts
protagonist.beliefs: Believes talent without leverage is just decorative suffering; wanted the promotion because without power, someone less competent will always decide your fate
protagonist.fears: Fears that if she pauses the velocity of her ambition for even forty-eight hours, she will collapse into the void left by her failed marriage and estranged family
protagonist.flaws: Translates all human relationships into transaction costs and leverage calculations; struggles to receive affection without suspecting an agenda
protagonist.speechStyle: Crisp, concise, uses active verbs, never raises voice in meetings, speaks with absolute economy
protagonist.secrets: Sat in the fire exit staircase of Tower 4B for forty minutes on Diwali night crying silently because she had nowhere to go before her 11 PM New York call
protagonist.memories: Her father's retirement day in 2012 when he was given a brass wall clock and a shawl after thirty-four years of checking vouchers, and swore she would never be discarded like that

secondaryCharacters.name: Sudhir Malhotra
secondaryCharacters.role: Former Senior Managing Director and Meera's institutional sponsor; ousted that same morning in a sudden boardroom reshuffle orchestrated by the London parent company
secondaryCharacters.significance: Represents the brutal shelf-life of executive power. His empty office at 7 PM with cardboard boxes is what Meera sees two hours after her promotion letter is signed.

secondaryCharacters.name: Ashwin Varma (Ex-Husband)
secondaryCharacters.role: Documentary filmmaker; left in 2023. Not a bad man, just someone who realized that being married to Meera meant living in the waiting room of someone else's emergency.

timeline.09:15 AM: Board meeting in Tower 4B; Sudhir Malhotra is quietly terminated; Meera is offered the Managing Director role with immediate operational oversight of 140 risk analysts across Gurgaon and Singapore.
timeline.01:30 PM: Meera signs the compensation addendum and non-compete extension. No hesitation; she has fought for this desk for eleven years.
timeline.05:00 PM: Company-wide email blast from global HR. 86 LinkedIn notifications, 42 Slack pings with celebration emojis.
timeline.07:30 PM: Sudhir leaves the building carrying his personal laptop and two potted ferns. His parting words to Meera: 'Don't mistake their panic for gratitude.'
timeline.09:00 PM: The office empties. Meera is alone on the 18th floor. A corporate floral bouquet from HR sits on her desk, smelling faintly of cold storage chemicals.
timeline.09:45 PM: Her phone is completely silent. No personal calls. Her mother in Thrissur had texted at 6 PM: 'Hope work is okay, calling tomorrow so as not to disturb your meetings.'
timeline.11:15 PM: Meera drives down Golf Course Road in her car. She stops at an all-night diner near Sector 54, ordering yellow dal and roti alone in the neon light. She calculates the ledger of her victory.

recurringMotifs: The 18th-floor executive glass wall looking out over the DLF golf course and the yellow ribbon of the expressway
The corporate floral bouquet with purple hydrangeas and white lilies wrapped in metallic plastic
The two phones—one corporate encrypted, one personal—the personal phone showing zero missed calls
Her father's brass retirement clock ticking on a mantelpiece in Thrissur
The glass jar of roasted almonds in her executive desk drawer
prohibitions: Do not make Meera regret her ambition in a moralistic or reactionary way; her drive is legitimate, earned, and intelligent
Do not suggest she should have 'chosen family instead' like a cliché sermon
The corporate world is depicted with clinical realism, not caricature villains; people are courteous, ruthless, and exhausted
The ending must capture the specific, cold dignity of solitary achievement
